502:
** ἄντλ-ημα**, ατος, τό,
**bucket for drawing water,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.974e, Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1332, NT.John.4.11.}}
503:
** ἀντοφθαλμ-έω**,
**look in the face, meet face to face,** ἀ. κατὰ πρόσωπον {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 18.46.12}}: hence, **defy, withstand,** τινί and πρός τινα, {{LXX|[prev. author] 1.17.3, 2.24.1, etc., cf. LXX.Wis.12.14}}; ἀ τῷ ἀνέμῳ, of a ship, {{NT+3rd c.AD+|NT.Act.27.15; πάθεσι 3rd c.AD: Longinus Rhetor 34.4.}}
511:
** ἀνώτερος**, α, ον,
_comparative_ _adjective_ from ἄνω (B), **upper, higher,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 496b35, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “Ars Rhetorica” 1.1, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Asin.” 9}}; ἐπιβουλῆς ἀ. γέγονεν got **the better of,**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|Nic.Dem. p.25 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator}}; _neuter_ as _adverb_, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 503b18}}; **above,** {{LXX|LXX.Lev.11.21}}; **earlier** in a book, {{NT+2nd c.BC+|NT.Heb.10.8, compare 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.1.1}}; **to a higher place,** {{NT|NT.Luke.14.10}}. _adverb_ ἀνωτέρω, see at {ἄνω}.
519:
** ἀπάγχω**,
**strangle, throttle,** ὁ μὲν λάε νεβρὸν ἀπάγχων{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 19.230; γαλῆν ἀ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 795, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Marius” 27, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Legal.” 11}}; ὃ μάλιστά μ᾽ ἀπάγχει **chokes** me **with anger,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 686:}} —_middle_, _aorist_ ἀπηγξάμην, and _passive_, **hang oneself, to be hanged,** {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th c.BC: Archilochus Lyricus 67, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.131, 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.43, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 465, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.125, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 130, etc.; ἐκ δένδρων 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.81; ὥστε μ᾽ ἀπάγχεσθ᾽}}**am ready to choke,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 988; ἀπάγξασθαι ῥηγνύμενος 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 2.20.31.}}
532:
** ἀπαρα-σκεύαστος**, ον,
= {ἀπαράσκευος}, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.9 (_comparative_), NT.2Cor.9.4, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 4.8.41}}. _adverb_ **-τως**{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica ad Alexandrum” 1430a3.}}
538:
** ἀπᾰτάω** [ᾰπ],
late _Ionic dialect_ **ἀπατ-έω** {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Syr.D.” 27 (_passive_)}}: _imperfect_ ἠπάτων{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 938, _Ionic dialect_ ἐξ-απάτασκον Oracle texts in 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1070:}}_future_ -ήσω: _aorist_ ἠπάτησα, _Ionic dialect_ ἀπ-{{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.344, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 500 (Lyric poetry)}}: _perfect_ ἠπάτηκα{{Refs|[prev. author] “Ph.” 929}}:—_passive_, _future_ ἀπατηθήσομαι{{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Analytica Priora” 67a38}}, compare (ἐξ-) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 436b, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 2.123}}; also in _middle_ form ἀπατήσομαι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 262a}}, (ἐξ-) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.3}}: _aorist_ ἠπατήθην{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 52e}}: _perfect_ ἠπάτημαι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.46, etc.}}: (ἀπάτη):—**cheat, deceive,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.97, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.139, etc.}}; **cheat** one's **hopes,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 462; οἷ᾽ ἠπάτηκας 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 929; κλέμματα.. ἂ τὸν πολέμιον ἀπατήσας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 5.9}}: _absolutely_, **to be deceptive** or **fallacious,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1376b28}}:—_passive_, **to be self-deceived, mistaken,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “Fragmenta.” 182, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 594, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 262a, etc.; ἔγνωκα.. φωτὸς ἠπατημένη 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 807}}; τί γὰρ οὐκ.. ἔρχεται ἀγγελίας ἀπατώμενο; comes not **belied by** the result? {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “El.” 170; ἀ. περί τι 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1368b22; περί τινος [prev. author] “Sens.” 442b8; ἀ. ταύτην τὴν ἀπάτην [prev. author] “Anthologia Graeca” 0.74a6}}; also ἀπατᾶσθαι ὡς.. **to be deceived into thinking** that.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 323a.}} —The _compound_ ἐξαπατάω is more common, especially in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus}} and _Attic dialect_ Prose; the simple Verb is used in {{LXX+2nd c.BC+|LXX.Gen.3.13, +others, but not by 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus}}, and is rare in later Greek, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.15d.}}
541:
** ἀπαύγ-ασμα**, ατος, τό,
**radiance, effulgence,** of light **beaming from** a luminous body, φωτὸς ἀϊδίου{{LXX+NT+1st c.AD+|LXX.Wis.7.26; δόξης NT.Heb.1.3, compare 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.337, +others, 3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 5.27, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus cited in 6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 775.15.}}
543:
** ἀπείθ-εια**, ἡ,
**disobedience,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 3.5.5, 1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis 9.41, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.24.24; υἱοὶ τῆς ἀπειθείας NT.Eph.5.7}}; later ἀπειθία, ἡ, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|“BGU” 747ii14 (2nd c.AD), etc., “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum”}}
555:
** ἀπέκ-δῠσις**, εως, ἡ,
**putting off** (like clothes), NT.Col.2.11.
558:
** ἀπελεύθερ-ος**, ὁ,
**restored to freedom,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ichn.” 193}}; **emancipated slave, freedman,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 930d; ἀ. τινος 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.10}}; opposed to δοῦλος and μέτοικος, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 1.10, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1278a2; ἀ. ἀφιέναι τινά 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.41: _metaphorically_, ἀ. κυρίου NT.1Cor.7.22}}:—_feminine_ ἀπελευθέρα, _Ionic dialect_ **ἀπελευθέρη**, ἡ, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιδημίαι” 5.75, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.19, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 59.18, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 436.}}
559:
**Ἀπελλῆς**, -οῦ, accusative -ῆν (MM, see word), ὁ
**Apelles**: Rom.16:10.†

587:
** ἀποδεκ-τός**, όν
(ή, όν probable reading in {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Ir.” p.60 W.)}}, **acceptable, welcome**, {{NT+1st c.AD+|“OGI” 441.100, NT.1Tim.2.3, 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 11.83, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.1061a}}: _comparative_ **-ότερος**{{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Eup.” 1 “Praef.”}} _adverb_ **-τως**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|“Anecdota Graeca - MSS. Bibl. Oxon.” 3.139, Scholia 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1680.}}
590:
** ἀπόδημ-ος**,
_Doric dialect_ **-δᾱμος**, ον, **away from one's country, abroad,** οὐκ ἀ. Ἀπόλλωνος τυχόντος{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.5, compare 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.799f, etc.}}; ἀ. ἐπέρχεσθαι **from abroad**, {{Refs|“CIG” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” “Corpus Inscriptionum Graecarum” 3344 A (from Smyrna)}}; ἀ. στρατεία{{Refs 5th c.BC+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Am.” 6: _metaphorically_, τῆς ἐμῆς γνώμης 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 17:—less _Attic dialect_ than ἔκδημος, 2nd c.AD: Moeris Grammaticus 143, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.177.}}
592:
** ἀποδιορ-ίζω**,
**mark off by dividing** or **defining,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1290b26}}; (i.e. ἑαυτούς) {{NT|NT.Jude.19.}}
597:
** ἀποθησαυρ-ίζω**,
**store, hoard up,** {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Sir.3.4, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 5.40, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 23; ἑαυτοῖς τι NT.1Tim.6.19}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 7.8.4, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 16.21.}}
